sources.entry: FS PDF Compressor - Free, private PDF compressor for macOS and Linux.

summary.one_liner: FS PDF Compressor is a free, open-source desktop app that compresses PDFs locally with Ghostscript for macOS, Linux, and Windows.
summary.what_it_does: The app compresses PDFs on the user's machine using bundled Ghostscript, so files are not uploaded to a website. You can drag and drop one PDF, several PDFs, or a folder into it. It offers balanced compression by default plus two optional quality profiles. It replaces the original file only when the compressed result is smaller, and an optional Keep original mode writes a separate compressed copy. An optional Drop Zone is a small desktop target for dropping PDFs without opening the main window. It also adds right-click actions in Finder, Windows Explorer, GNOME Files, and KDE Dolphin. The README states that the app has no accounts, analytics, or telemetry, and that network access is limited to update delivery and links the user opens.
use_cases: batch compress a folder of PDFs
compress PDFs without uploading to a website
reduce PDF size from Finder or Explorer right-click menu
keep a compressed copy alongside originals
notable: Runs fully locally; no uploads, accounts, or telemetry
Bundles Ghostscript so users do not need a separate install
Replaces the original only when the output is smaller
Drop Zone desktop shortcut with per-platform behavior
macOS build is Developer ID signed and notarized
caveats: macOS build requires Apple Silicon and macOS 14+; Linux build is x86_64 only; Windows build is x64 Windows 11
Windows installer is currently unsigned and Windows updates are manual
Drop Zone may not pin to the desktop under Wayland on Linux
